title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative:
To bring about the realisation of human rights for poor and marginalised men and women affected by high inequality, human rights violations and violence in seven conflict or post-conflict countries by addressing issues of governance, tackling violence, building peace and promoting equality for all, particularly gender equality. Outcome 1.1: Israeli and Palestinian laws, policies and practices are less discriminatory (for example displacement, denial of services and economic marginalisation) and more inclusive. Outcome 1.2: The lives of Palestinians have improved as there is reduced discrimination such as reduced displacement, increased freedom of movement (goods and people), and increased civic space for Palestinians to demand their rights.
Outcome 1.3: International bodies hold the Israeli Government to account for human rights violations (for example forced displacement, arbitrary arrest) in breach of IHL/IHRL. Objective 1: Marginalised women and men realise their human rights by having more equitable access to land, housing, basic services and secure livelihoods, benefit from progressive taxes and fiscal policies and actively participate as citizens and influence decisions that affect their lives.
